segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Today was supposed to be Thanksgiving.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: You remembered waking up thinking about mashed potatoes, pumpkin pie, and watching football with your family. You remembered the desert air being cool and dry, like it always was in November in Arizona.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: You definitely did not expect this.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: You press your forehead against the glass of your bedroom window. Outside, towering Saguaro cacti look like giant green snowmen, shivering under three feet of heavy, freezing snow. Icicles hang from the telephone wires like glittering fangs.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And down on the sidewalk, marching in perfect, stiff-legged unison, are soldiers.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Not real soldiers. They are made of polished, painted wood. They wear bright red coats with gold buttons, tall black fuzzy hats, and giant white grins that never, ever close. Their wooden jaws click with every step:

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Clack-clack. Clack-clack.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: When you went downstairs this morning, your family wasn’t in the kitchen cooking turkey. They were gathered around a glittering, twelve-foot pine tree that definitely hadn't been there yesterday. They were singing carols with wide, glassy eyes, humming along to music that seemed to be drifting out of the floorboards.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: When you asked your mom what happened to Thanksgiving, she just smiled a strange, faraway smile.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Thanksgiving? Don't be silly, sweetheart. It’s Christmas morning. It’s always been Christmas morning.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Something inside your chest twisted. You knew—with total, stubborn certainty—that yesterday was Wednesday, November twenty-seventh. But nobody else seemed to remember yesterday at all.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then the wooden soldiers knocked on your front door.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The soldiers marched you through the snowy streets straight to your school.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Except Oak Creek Elementary didn't look like school anymore. The double doors were flanked by giant peppermint candy canes, and a painted banner over the entrance read:

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: DISTRICT 4 MERRIMENT PROCESSING STATION — ENJOY YOUR CHEER.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Inside, the warm smell of floor wax and basketballs was completely buried under an overwhelming stench of burnt peppermint and cinnamon. The gymnasium scoreboard above the bleachers flickered with bright red numbers: DEC 25.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Along the baseline, a dozen children stood in a nervous line. At the front of the line, your best friends, Maya and Leo, were huddled together in their winter coats.

segments.speaker: hero
segments.text: Hey!

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: you whisper, slipping up behind them.

segments.speaker: hero
segments.text: Maya! Leo! What is going on?

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Maya turns, her eyes wide with panic.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: They rounded up everyone who didn't come out of their houses to sing carols! They said we have an acute case of 'Holiday Irregularity'!

segments.speaker: pip
segments.text: They're putting people in front of that thing,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Leo whispers, pointing a shaking mitten toward the center court.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Where the center jump circle used to be sat a massive iron stove—the Cheer Hearth. Its copper pipes rattled and hissed, venting sweet-smelling, glittery lavender steam into the gym rafters. Inside the hearth, a flame danced with a strange, hypnotic purple-and-gold glow.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: A towering Nutcracker commander with brass epaulets slammed his wooden staff onto the floor.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: THUMP!

segments.speaker: soldier
segments.text: NEXT CITIZEN,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: the commander boomed, his painted wooden lips snapping open and shut.

segments.speaker: soldier
segments.text: PROCEED TO THE CHEER HEARTH TO RESTORE MANDATORY FESTIVE SPIRIT.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Two wooden guards grabbed Maya by the elbows.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Wait! Let go of me!

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Maya cried, pulling back.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Today is Thanksgiving! I'm supposed to visit my grandma!

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The guards didn't blink. They forced Maya onto a small brass stool directly in front of the swirling purple fire.

segments.speaker: hero
segments.text: Maya!

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: you shout, taking a step forward, but a wooden bayonet snaps down, blocking your path.

segments.speaker: soldier
segments.text: OBSERVE,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: the Nutcracker guard rattles.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: THE SPIRIT RESTORATION IS COMMENCING.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The lavender smoke from the hearth coiled gently around Maya’s face like warm ribbons. For a second, she squeezed her eyes shut, fighting it. You could see her trying to hold on to her memories—trying to remember her family, her grandma, the world that was here just yesterday.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then, her shoulders relaxed.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The fear in her face melted away. Her eyes opened, but the spark in them was gone, replaced by a smooth, glossy reflection of the purple flame.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: A calm, gentle smile spread across her lips.

segments.speaker: hero
segments.text: Maya?

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: you whisper, your voice trembling.

segments.speaker: hero
segments.text: Do you hear me?

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Maya looked straight at you, blinking slowly. Her voice was smooth and polite, like someone reciting lines from a holiday greeting card.

segments.speaker: maya
segments.text: Why are you looking so worried?

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: she asked pleasantly.

segments.speaker: maya
segments.text: Isn't it wonderful? It's Christmas. We're going to open presents all day.

segments.speaker: hero
segments.text: No, Maya, listen to me,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: you plead.

segments.speaker: hero
segments.text: It’s Thanksgiving. Think about yesterday!

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Maya let out a soft, tinkling laugh that made the hair on your arms stand up.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Yesterday? There is no yesterday. There is only Christmas.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The commander stepped forward, stamping Maya's hand with a glowing red snowflake ink stamp.

segments.speaker: soldier
segments.text: PROCESSED. ASSIGN CITIZEN TO REINDEER CRAFTS.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The commander slowly turned his painted, unblinking black eyes toward you.

segments.speaker: soldier
segments.text: NEXT SUBJECT,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: the commander clicked.

segments.speaker: soldier
segments.text: YOU ARE DEMONSTRATING SEVERE CHEER RESISTANCE. STEP FORWARD.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: You look at the glowing hearth. You feel a strange hum in the back of your mind—a quiet, stubborn voice telling you that you are different. The magic that took Maya’s memories washes against your thoughts, but it doesn't take hold. It slides off like water on glass.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: You remember the truth. And if you go up to that hearth, there's no telling if you can hold on to it.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: You need to run. Now.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The wooden guards step toward you, their joints creaking in rhythm. Clack-clack. Clack-clack.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: You have about three seconds before wooden hands grab your coat. You scan the gymnasium for a way out:

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The three soldiers closing in have little copper gears visible behind their ears, twitching in sync with the holiday music.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: To your left, the shadow under the folded wooden bleachers offers a low crawl space toward the equipment room.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: To your right, a twenty-foot pyramid of oversized, red-and-gold gift boxes stands directly between you and the side emergency exit.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: What do you do?

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: You take a deep breath, puff out your chest, and belt out at the top of your lungs:

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: JINGLE BELLS! JINGLE BELLS! JINGLE ALL THE—

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: You clamp your mouth shut.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Instantly, all three soldiers freeze mid-step. Their painted wooden jaws drop wide open. Inside their chests, copper gears grind and screech in agony as their internal programming violently collides with the unfinished tune.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: WHIRRRR-CLICK-SPUTTER!

segments.speaker: soldier
segments.text: CANNOT PERMIT... UNFINISHED CADENCE...

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: the commander chokes out.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Compelled by ancient holiday magic, the soldiers snap their heels together, raise their arms in stiff choreography, and burst into a deafening, mechanical three-part barbershop harmony:

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: —WAAAAAY! OH WHAT FUN IT IS TO RIDE IN A ONE-HORSE OPEN SLEIIIIIGH!

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: While the soldiers are locked in their four-part vibrato, completely powerless to stop singing, you sprint right under their wooden noses, barrel through the emergency doors, and burst out into the freezing alley!

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: You hit the varnished wood floor and slide on your stomach right beneath the bottom row of folded wooden bleachers!

segments.speaker: soldier
segments.text: TARGET HAS VACATED VISUAL FIELD!

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: a soldier clicks above you. Heavy wooden boots stomp on the floorboards inches from your fingers. THUD-THUD-THUD!

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The space under the bleachers is dark, smelling of dust and lost tennis balls. You keep your head down and scramble on your elbows and knees through the crisscrossing metal support bars. Up above, the soldiers are marching back and forth, knocking over folding chairs in confusion.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: At the far end of the bleachers, you spot the propped-open equipment room door. You wriggle through a row of red rubber dodgeballs, slide past the ball carts, kick open the back service exit, and dive out into the biting winter air!

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: You grab the thick velvet ribbon dangling from the bottom of the twenty-foot gift box display and give it everything you've got!

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: RIPPPPP!

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The bottom box slips out, and the entire festive mountain groans.

segments.speaker: soldier
segments.text: CRITICAL STRUCTURAL FAILURE!

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: the commander rattles, waving his arms.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: A shower of colossal, brightly wrapped boxes collapses across the gym like a bright red tidal wave! Giant velvet bows, Styrofoam packing peanuts, and heavy cardboard boxes crash down on the soldiers, sweeping them off their wooden feet.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The soldiers slide across the polished gym floor like bowling pins, their legs spinning in the air.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: CRASH! BANG! CLATTER!

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Using the tumbling boxes as stepping stones, you sprint across the floor, smash your shoulder against the emergency push-bar, and burst through the heavy metal doors into the blinding snow!

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The cold air hits your lungs like ice water.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: You slam the heavy metal emergency door behind you and lean against it, panting. Arizona shouldn't feel like the North Pole, but the wind howling down the alley cuts straight through your jacket.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Behind the metal door, you hear angry wooden fists hammering on the steel:

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: BAM! BAM! BAM!

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: FESTIVE RESISTER DETECTED! DEPLOYING PURSUIT CONTINGENT!

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: You look down the alley. Towering brick walls hem you in on both sides. Deep snowdrifts block the path to the street, and green garbage dumpsters are covered in foot-thick mounds of snow. You need somewhere to hide, and fast.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Suddenly, the air in the center of the alley begins to crackle.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: It sounds like popping sugar and ticking clock gears. A circle of brilliant, blinding light—glowing warm gold and glacial blue—tears open in the empty air three feet above the ground. Frost crystals spin wildly inside the opening like a miniature hurricane.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Before you can even blink, something comes tumbling out of the portal.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: FLUMP!

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: It lands directly upside-down in the biggest snowdrift next to the green dumpster.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The portal snaps shut with a sound like a closing pocket watch.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: For three seconds, the alley is dead silent. The only thing moving is a bushy, reddish-orange tail with a snow-covered white tip, sticking straight up out of the snowbank and twitching with great indignation.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: With a muffled grunt and a flurry of powdery snow, the figure yanks its head out of the drift.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: It’s a fox. A real, living, three-foot-tall fox standing on two hind paws.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He wears a heavy green detective's coat that is clearly three sizes too big for him, with brass buttons the size of saucers. A long, hand-knitted red wool scarf is wrapped around his neck so many times his snout barely pokes over the top, and a crooked tweed detective hat rests lopsidedly between two pointed, velvet-brown ears.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The fox shakes the snow off his whiskers, vigorously brushes white powder off his coat lapels, and clears his throat with great theatrical flair.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: When he speaks, his voice is surprisingly deep, carrying a ridiculously posh, exaggerated British accent:

segments.speaker: pip
segments.text: Ahem! Splendid! An absolutely immaculate piece of trans-dimensional navigation. Father Christmas, I presume, should be standing precisely—

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The fox pauses. His yellow eyes slowly travel across the brick wall, the icy gravel, and settle directly on the rusted green dumpster three feet from his nose.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He squints at the graffiti on the dumpster lid.

segments.speaker: pip
segments.text: Ah,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: he murmurs, his ears drooping slightly.

segments.speaker: pip
segments.text: That is... mildly disappointing. The North Pole appears to have significantly deferred its exterior maintenance.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Down the alleyway, around the corner of the gym, you hear the sharp, rhythmic crunch of wooden boots on frozen snow:

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Crunch-clack. Crunch-clack.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The Nutcracker pursuit patrol is coming.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: What do you do?

segments.speaker: pip
segments.text: Hey!

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: you hiss from the shadows by the brick wall.

segments.speaker: pip
segments.text: Get down! The wooden soldiers are right around the corner!

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The fox jumps three feet straight into the air, his tail poofing out to the size of a water heater!

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: His fancy British accent vanishes in an instant.

segments.speaker: hero
segments.text: SWEET MOTHER OF GINGERBREAD, HALT! I'M ARMED! I DON'T KNOW WHAT THIS DOES!

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He spins around in the snow, wildly swinging a heavy, gleaming brass device in both paws like a club.

segments.speaker: hero
segments.text: Shh! Be quiet!

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: you whisper, lunging forward and waving your hands.

segments.speaker: hero
segments.text: I'm trying to help you!

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The fox blinks, lowers the brass device slightly, and quickly adjusts his crooked detective cap. He straightens his posture and his ridiculous accent returns as if nothing happened:

segments.speaker: pip
segments.text: Ahem. Yes. Quite. Naturally, I was merely... testing your tactical reflexes. You passed with acceptable marks, civilian.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Keeping your boots light on the snow, you creep around the corner of the brick wall to get a better look at what he's holding.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: In his furry paws, the fox is clutching an extraordinary contraption. It looks like a giant, pocket-watch-sized compass forged from polished brass and dark copper. Beneath a spiderweb-cracked crystal face, half a dozen tiny silver needles are spinning erratically in opposite directions. Tiny glass vials of glowing blue sand bubble on the sides, and interlocking gears click softly: tick-tick-tick-whirr.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: As you lean in closer, your shadow falls across him.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The fox's ears shoot up. He wheels around, dropping his accent completely:

segments.speaker: pip
segments.text: YAAAAAH! BACK OFF! I'LL PRESS THE BUTTON! I SWEAR TO ST. NICK I'LL PRESS IT!

segments.speaker: hero
segments.text: Wait, don't yell!

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: you whisper, holding up your hands.

segments.speaker: hero
segments.text: I'm running from the Nutcrackers!

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The fox halts, eyeing your winter jacket suspiciously. He clears his throat, tucks the device under his arm, and pulls on his lapels.

segments.speaker: pip
segments.text: Ahem. Of course. A fellow fugitive from justice. I deduced that instantly from the aerodynamic angle of your shoelaces.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: There’s no time to explain. The beam of a Nutcracker's brass lantern is already sweeping across the brick wall fifty feet away.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: You sprint forward, grab the trailing tail of the fox's long red scarf, and give it a firm yank!

segments.speaker: pip
segments.text: I SAY! UNHAND THE MERCHANDISE—OOF!

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: You pull the fox sideways behind the wide green dumpster just as the lantern beam cuts through the snow where he was standing!

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The fox lands on your boots, his cap knocked down over his eyes. For a second, he panics in pure, unscripted terror:

segments.speaker: pip
segments.text: I DON'T TASTE GOOD! I'M MOSTLY FLUFF AND BAD ATTITUDE!

segments.speaker: hero
segments.text: Quiet!

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: you whisper into his furry ear, pointing toward the mouth of the alley.

segments.speaker: hero
segments.text: Look.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Peering through the gap between the dumpster and the wall, the fox watches as four stiff-legged Nutcrackers march past, their brass bayonets gleaming in the snow.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The fox pushes his hat out of his eyes. He looks at you, looks at the soldiers, and nods with dignified gravity:

segments.speaker: pip
segments.text: Ahem. An adequate flanking maneuver. I allowed you to execute it to bolster your youthful self-esteem. You may thank me later.

segments.speaker: pip
segments.text: SUSPICIOUS SCARF RESIDUE IDENTIFIED,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: a metallic voice clicks from the snow.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: You and the fox freeze.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: One of the Nutcracker soldiers has stopped right in front of the dumpster. Its wooden head slowly rotates a full one-hundred-and-eighty degrees backward, until its unblinking black eyes lock directly onto you and the fox.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: CLACK-CLACK.

segments.speaker: soldier
segments.text: UNAUTHORIZED CANINE DETECTED,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: the soldier rattles.

segments.speaker: soldier
segments.text: UNRECONSTRUCTED YOUTH DETECTED. SURRENDER FOR IMMEDIATE FESTIVE INTEGRATION.

segments.speaker: pip
segments.text: Festive integration?!

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: the fox gasps, his fur standing straight on end.

segments.speaker: pip
segments.text: I'll have you know I am already exceedingly festive! I once wore mistletoe in my tail for three consecutive fortnights!

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Five more soldiers round the corner, raising wooden staffs that hum with crackling violet electricity. They box you into the brick wall. There's nowhere left to run.

segments.speaker: hero
segments.text: Alright, clever guy,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: you say, looking down at the fox.

segments.speaker: hero
segments.text: You're a detective? What's the plan?

segments.speaker: pip
segments.text: The plan?

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The fox laughs, a high-pitched, nervous sound that squeaks like a rusty hinge.

segments.speaker: pip
segments.text: The plan is elementary! We employ the ancient art of... OH GINGER-SNAPS, WE'RE GOING TO BE FIREWOOD!

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: His British accent is completely gone now.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He frantically grabs the brass compass, violently shaking it like an old ketchup bottle.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Work, you blasted pile of clockwork! Work!

segments.speaker: hero
segments.text: What does it do?!

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: you shout as the soldiers close in, their painted teeth grinning.

segments.speaker: pip
segments.text: I DON'T KNOW! I FOUND IT IN THE CLOCK TOWER!

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The fox raises his furry paw and slams his palm down onto the large copper plunger on top of the compass!

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: CLIIIIICK-WHIRRRRRR!

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Inside the brass casing, the spinning gears scream. The spiderweb cracks on the glass face erupt with blinding, glacial-blue light!

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: A freezing shockwave of wind explodes through the alley, blowing the soldiers' fuzzy hats straight off their wooden heads!

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The brick walls seem to bend like rubber. The snowy ground drops out from beneath your boots. Before you can scream, the blue light twists into a roaring vortex of frost, gears, and temporal lightning—swallowing you and the fox whole!

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: WHHOOOOOOOOOOSH!

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: You crash into something soft, cold, and utterly blinding.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Snow. Tons and tons of freezing, powdery, delicious-smelling snow.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: You roll over, sputtering and coughing, shaking white flakes out of your eyelashes. The biting Arizona wind is gone. The smell of asphalt and garbage dumpsters is gone. Instead, the air smells crisp and magical—like fresh pine needles, woodsmoke, peppermint, and melted chocolate.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Next to you in the drift, the brass compass gives a tired little pfffft sound, and a sad wisp of black smoke curls out from its gears.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: A pair of pointed ears pops out of the snow, followed by a tweed hat.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Pip sits up, rubs his sore nose, and adjusts his coat with trembling paws. He glances at the broken, smoking compass, quickly stuffs it behind his back, and clears his throat:

segments.speaker: pip
segments.text: Ahem. And thus concludes our rapid tactical repositioning. Text-book execution. Nothing to it.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He turns to look at you, his eyes darting around nervously.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: You wouldn't, by any remote stretch of the imagination... happen to know how to repair an eighth-century chronometric flux-spring, would you?

segments.speaker: hero
segments.text: No,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: you say, brushing snow off your knees.

segments.speaker: hero
segments.text: Where are we?

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Pip doesn't answer right away. He slowly turns around, looking down the ridge.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: You follow his gaze—and your breath catches in your throat.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Spread across the valley below is the most extraordinary village you have ever seen.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Hundreds of gingerbread-trimmed cottages nestle against the snowy mountainside, their frosted windows glowing with warm, welcoming amber light. Frozen waterways of glittering ice wind under carved stone bridges, and hot-air balloons decorated like holiday ornaments drift lazily between mountain peaks.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And rising high above the center of the village, towering into the starry sky, is the Grand Clock.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: It is an immense, breathtaking mountain of brass, crystal, and glowing clockwork. Towering gear wheels five stories high turn in silent, majestic harmony, bathing the entire valley in a soft, golden radiance.

segments.speaker: pip
segments.text: Welcome,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Pip whispers, his voice quiet and uncharacteristically solemn.

segments.speaker: pip
segments.text: To Everfrost.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: You stare down at the glowing spires.

segments.speaker: pip
segments.text: Everfrost? What is this place?

segments.speaker: pip
segments.text: It's where Christmas comes from,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Pip says, clutching his coat tighter around his chest.

segments.speaker: pip
segments.text: Or rather... where it is supposed to be kept safe.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Suddenly, the golden glow from the giant clock flickers.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Deep inside the clockwork spires, something groans. A metallic shriek echoes across the valley, so loud it sends snow avalanching down the distant peaks.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The massive, golden hour hand on the Grand Clock violently shudders.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Instead of moving forward... it jerks backward.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: BONGGGGGGG.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: A deep, unnatural bell tolls across the village.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: BONG. BONG. BONG.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: You count the strikes in your head. Nine... ten... eleven... twelve...

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: BONG.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Thirteen.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: A cold, violet wave of magical energy ripples outward from the clock tower, sweeping across the village roofs. In an instant, every warm amber window in Everfrost blinks out into darkness.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Pip’s bushy tail drops between his legs. His eyes go wide with genuine horror.

segments.speaker: hero

segments.text: You spot three items within arm's reach on the workbench:

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: An antique sprig of polished brass mistletoe with tiny jingle bells.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: A beautifully wrapped, empty red holiday gift box with an elaborate golden silk bow.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: A pair of long iron clock-tweezers right next to the soldiers' spinning back-keys.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: What silly trick do you use to stop the Nutcrackers?

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: You grab the brass mistletoe off the workbench and thrust it high above your head!

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: JINGLE-JINGLE!

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Instantly, the three soldiers freeze mid-stride. Their wooden jaws snap open, their glass eyes dilating in sheer panic.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: BUZZZZ-CLICK-SPUTTER!

segments.speaker: soldier
segments.text: CRITICAL PROTOCOL OVERRIDE!

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: the lead soldier chokes out with a mechanical shudder.

segments.speaker: soldier
segments.text: MISTLETOE DETECTED OVERHEAD! MILITARY HOSTILITIES SUSPENDED! INITIATE MANDATORY FESTIVE COURTESY!

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Compelled by ancient holiday law, the soldiers drop their wooden shock-staves. The three giant wooden sentries turn to each other, bow stiffly at the waist, and begin exchanging absurdly polite holiday compliments:

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: YOU LOOK EXCEPTIONALLY RADIANT THIS AFTERNOON, SERGEANT CRACKER!

segments.speaker: pip
segments.text: NO, SERGEANT, YOUR GOLD BUTTONS ARE BY FAR THE SUPERIOR ADORNMENT!

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: While the soldiers are locked in an endless loop of frantic, aggressive hugging and bowing, you grab Pip’s paw and sprint past them!

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: You snatch the shiny red holiday box off the desk and shove it directly into the lead soldier’s outstretched wooden hands!

segments.speaker: soldier
segments.text: GIFT DELIVERY DETECTED!

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: the soldier announces with alarming cheerfulness.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The soldier’s wooden fingers snap tightly around the ribbon. His pupils spin like tiny clockwork roulette wheels as his programming locks up:

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: WHIRRR-CLICK!

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: COMMENCING FOUR-HUNDRED-POINT HOLIDAY PACKAGING EVALUATION. CRITERIA ONE: IS THE GOLDEN BOW POSITIONED AT A PRECISE FORTY-FIVE-DEGREE FESTIVE INCLINE?

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The other two soldiers immediately drop their weapons, pull tiny wooden rulers and brass magnifying glasses from their coats, and crowd around the box, loudly debating the tension of the wrapping paper:

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: THE HOSPITALITY CREASE ON THE NORTHEAST CORNER IS CLEARLY DEFICIENT BY THREE MILLIMETERS!

segments.speaker: pip
segments.text: NONSENSE, LIEUTENANT! THE RIBBON DENSITY PASSES ROYAL INSPECTION!

segments.speaker: pip
segments.text: Great Scott!

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Pip gasps, tiptoeing behind you.

segments.speaker: pip
segments.text: They're arguing over gift-wrap! Move, move, move!

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: You grab the heavy iron clock-tweezers and slide like a hockey player across the slick river stones, ducking right behind the lead Nutcracker!

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: With a quick, sharp twist of the tweezers, you jam the tool into the brass ratchet gear beneath the soldier's giant back-key and FLIP the switch!

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: SPRRR-IIII-NNNG!

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The massive golden key violently reverses direction!

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The soldier’s wooden head spins a full three-hundred-and-sixty degrees on his neck. His legs begin marching backward with double the speed:

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: CLACK-CLACK-CLACK!

segments.speaker: soldier
segments.text: !TLAAAH! !RETSISER EVITSEF ,EERETNES ERAPERP!

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: the soldier bellows in complete backward reverse, furiously moonwalking across the vault floor!

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He crashes straight into the second soldier, whose key also catches and flips in reverse! Within seconds, all three soldiers are furiously marching backward in a tangled, chaotic pile of red coats, wooden boots, and fuzzy hats, tumbling backward right up the stone stairs like a herd of confused dominoes!

segments.speaker: pip
segments.text: A masterstroke of chronological reversal!

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Pip crows.

segments.speaker: pip
segments.text: Run!

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Behind the workbench, you spot a vertical maintenance shaft. An old iron ladder runs straight up through the rock, leading toward a faint square of snowy moonlight high above.

segments.speaker: hero
segments.text: Up the ladder!

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: you shout.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: You and Pip scramble up the iron rungs as fast as you can. You climb past the thundering, frozen waterwheel shaft, bursting through an old sheet-metal trapdoor out onto the pitched roof of the Old Mill!

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The freezing mountain wind hits you like a slap. Snow is falling thick and heavy across the wooden shingles.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: You scramble up to the roof peak—and stop dead in your tracks.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Down in the courtyard below, the mill is completely surrounded.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Dozens of Nutcracker soldiers on clockwork horses have ringed the building. Their brass searchlights sweep across the snowy roof, pinning you and Pip in a blinding crossfire of white light.

segments.speaker: pip
segments.text: SURRENDER THE C.M. JOURNAL!

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: a loudspeaker horn blares from the ground.

segments.speaker: pip
segments.text: THERE IS NO ESCAPE FROM FESTIVE ORDER!

segments.speaker: pip
segments.text: We're trapped,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: you pant, looking at the forty-foot drop into the frozen river.

segments.speaker: pip
segments.text: Pip, there's nowhere to go!

segments.speaker: pip
segments.text: Nonsense!

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Pip declared, puffing out his coat and reaching into his inner pocket with supreme, triumphant flair.

segments.speaker: pip
segments.text: Master Detective Pip never enters a hornets' nest without an aerial tactical evacuation strategy!

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He pulled out a heavy brass whistle shaped like an acorn.

segments.speaker: pip
segments.text: Behold! The Emergency Sky-Howler! I am about to summon Everfrost's most ferocious aerial transport operative! A creature of raw power, iron discipline, and blood-curdling sky-courage!

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Pip put the whistle to his lips and blew with all his might.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: No sound came out. Just a high-pitched, ultrasonic hiss that made your teeth vibrate.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: For five seconds, nothing happened.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then, the snowy clouds directly above the mill began to glow.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Parting the swirling storm clouds, an enormous, magnificent hot-air balloon descended out of the sky.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The balloon envelope was colossal—shaped like a round holiday ornament made of thick, quilted canvas with vibrant red-and-white peppermint stripes. Hanging beneath the burner was an oversized wicker gondola reinforced with polished copper pipes and brass fog lamps.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The balloon drifted down toward the roof peak, its twin propane burners roaring: WHOOOOOOSH!

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Standing at the brass steering helm of the basket was the pilot.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: You blink in disbelief.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He was an American Bulldog. But not just any bulldog—he was a towering, broad-chested powerhouse of a dog with massive muscular shoulders, a big square head, and a brilliant white coat sprinkled with tiny black freckles across his muzzle and ears. He wore a shearling-lined leather bomber jacket, a fleece-lined aviator cap, and a pair of brass flight goggles perched over two big, soulful, chocolate-brown eyes. His little docked tail was clamped down tight in nervousness.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: When he stepped up to the edge of the basket, he looked so big and formidable that the Nutcrackers on the ground actually paused their marching in sheer intimidation.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then the wicker basket bumped the mill chimney with a gentle thud.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The giant bulldog let out a sharp, pathetic squeak:

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: EEP!

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He dropped flat onto his belly in the bottom of the basket, threw both of his massive, muscular white paws over his ears, and began shivering so violently the entire gondola rattled!

segments.speaker: titan
segments.text: O-Oh goodness! Oh crumpets and cocoa!

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: the bulldog whimpered in a deep, booming voice that sounded like a giant bag of rocks being gently shaken.

segments.speaker: titan
segments.text: Tell me it was just a chimney! Tell me it wasn't an airborne snow-monster! Pip! Pip, are you down there?! I am having a medical crisis of pure fear!

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Pip scrambled across the snowy roof and grabbed the rim of the basket.

segments.speaker: pip
segments.text: Titan! Pull yourself together, man! We are under active hostile fire!

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The bulldog peeked one eye out from under his spotted ear. He spotted you, gasped, and tried to squeeze his giant body behind a tiny sandbag:

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: A human?! A real human?! D-Do they bite?! Are they dangerous?!

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Down on the ground, the Nutcracker soldiers recovered from their shock and raised their brass staves!

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: CRACK-CRACK-CRACK!

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Luminous webs of sticky, glowing silver tinsel nets shot upward from the courtyard, latching onto the mill gutters and tearing toward the balloon basket!

segments.speaker: pip
segments.text: Titan!

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Pip screamed, diving over the wicker rim.

segments.speaker: pip
segments.text: Engage the burners! Fly, you glorious coward, FLY!

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: You scramble over the edge of the basket, tumbling onto the fleece floorboards right next to the giant shivering bulldog.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: I can't!

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Titan wailed, his big black-spotted jowls flapping as he buried his face in his paws.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: My paws are like jelly! The wind is windy! The dark is dark! My emotional constitution is compromised!

segments.speaker: hero
segments.text: Titan, they're shooting nets at us!

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: you yell, pointing over the side.

segments.speaker: pip
segments.text: I need emotional support!

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Titan bellowed softly.

segments.speaker: pip
segments.text: Pip! Did you bring them?! Tell me you remembered the emergency ration!

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Pip froze. His eyes went wide. He patted his empty pockets in frantic despair.

segments.speaker: pip
segments.text: The nubbies!

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Pip shrieked.

segments.speaker: pip
segments.text: I left the bacon-and-cheddar nubbies on my tea desk!

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Titan let out a devastating, heartbroken whimper that could have melted an iceberg.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: THWACK!

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: A silver tinsel net snapped onto the bottom of the wicker basket, dragging the balloon downward toward the roof!

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: You look at your winter jacket. When you escaped your house in Arizona this morning, your mom had put a small plastic baggie in your pocket for your family's puppy: crunchy, star-shaped holiday dog biscuits.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: You rip open your pocket.

segments.speaker: hero
segments.text: Titan!

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: you shout, holding up a golden, crunchy star-shaped biscuit right in front of his big black nose.

segments.speaker: hero
segments.text: LOOK!

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Titan’s droopy eyes snapped open. His nostrils flared like two jet engines.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: SNIIIIIIIIFFFF.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Is that...

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Titan whispered, his little docked tail giving a sudden, hopeful twitch.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: ...an artisanal, oven-baked poultry-and-herb nubbie?

segments.speaker: hero
segments.text: It’s Thanksgiving turkey flavor,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: you say.

segments.speaker: hero
segments.text: And the whole bag is yours—plus as many ear scratches as you want—if you get us into the sky right now!

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Scratches?!

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Titan gasped, his eyes shining like Christmas morning.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Ear scratches AND nubbies?!

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Titan’s posture changed in half a second.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: His eyes locked onto the burner handle. With a ferocious, thunderous snort of pure determination, the giant American Bulldog rose on his hind legs, seized the brass burner throttle with both paws, and yanked it all the way down!

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: ROOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOAR!

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: A twin pillar of brilliant blue-and-gold flame blasted into the peppermint balloon!

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The tinsel nets snapped like thread! The basket surged straight up into the snowy sky, leaving the shouting Nutcrackers and their flashing searchlights shrinking into tiny dots on the snowy ground below!

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The roaring wind faded to a peaceful, freezing hum as the peppermint balloon leveled off high above Everfrost.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Below you, the village looked like a dark fairy-tale kingdom carved from ice and shadow. Snow-capped roofs and frozen canals wound through the valley under a sky dancing with emerald and violet auroras. In the distance, the Grand Clock stood like a silent mountain of brass, its pendulum still swinging in cold, ominous silence.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Titan was leaning his massive, ninety-pound head directly against your knee, letting out contented snorts as you vigorously scratched the sweet spot right behind his black-speckled ears. His little docked tail was buzzing back and forth so fast it was a white blur against the wicker basket.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: CRUNCH-MUNCH-CRUNCH.

segments.speaker: pip
segments.text: You are an angel,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Titan sighed, swallowing another turkey nubbie and leaning his heavy weight affectionately against your legs.

segments.speaker: pip
segments.text: A small, coat-wearing angel of savory treats and elite scratching technique. I would fly into a volcano for you. As long as the volcano was kept at a comfortable, non-scary temperature.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Pip leaned against the brass railing, his trench coat blowing in the wind, his fancy British accent fully restored:

segments.speaker: pip
segments.text: Ahem. An adequate extraction, Titan. Slightly lacking in military decorum, but acceptable.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Pip pulled the thick, leather-bound journal of C.M. from his coat and laid it across an oak navigation chest.

segments.speaker: pip
segments.text: Now then,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Pip said solemnly.

segments.speaker: pip
segments.text: We must decipher the Clockmaker’s notes. The clock has struck twelve. Time is running backward. We need to know how to stop the primary escapement before Christmas Day.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Titan leaned his massive head over the table, squinting through his flight goggles at the gold-embossed letters on the cover: C.M.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Titan gasped. His little docked tail froze.

segments.speaker: pip
segments.text: Sweet mother of gravy...

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Titan whispered, his jowls quivering.

segments.speaker: pip
segments.text: That’s Barnaby's master's journal.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: You and Pip both turn to look at him.

segments.speaker: hero
segments.text: Who is Barnaby?

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: you ask.

segments.speaker: pip
segments.text: Barnaby Grumble,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Titan whispered, looking nervously at the clouds as if someone might be listening.

segments.speaker: pip
segments.text: The old master clock-smith. Centurys ago, before Everfrost was built, Barnaby was the Clockmaker's only apprentice. He helped forge the original gears.

segments.speaker: pip
segments.text: An apprentice?!

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Pip shouted, his tail bristling.

segments.speaker: pip
segments.text: Where is he?! Why haven't I found him?!

segments.speaker: pip
segments.text: Because he's in hiding!

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Titan said.

segments.speaker: pip
segments.text: When the Clockmaker started going mad with jealousy, Barnaby tried to warn Santa. The Clockmaker locked Barnaby out, and now the Nutcrackers are hunting him. He's holed up in the Clockwork Scrap-Junkyard in the East Chasm. Nobody goes there. It's full of broken toys, guard traps, and... and spooky noises!

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Titan shivered, whimpered, and leaned all of his heavy weight into your lap for comfort.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: You smile, giving his big blocky head another warm scratch, and look out through the clouds at the jagged, icy peaks of the East Chasm.

segments.speaker: hero
segments.text: Titan,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: you say gently.

segments.speaker: hero
segments.text: Turn the balloon toward the East Chasm. We're going to meet Barnaby.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The peppermint balloon drifted down through the swirling snow of the East Chasm.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The canyon walls were sheer cliffs of jagged black rock, but the canyon floor looked like an explosion in a colossal clock factory. Centuries of discarded machinery were piled fifty feet high: rusted iron balance wheels, giant brass pendulums, snapped springs, and mountains of hollow toy parts half-buried in the snow.

segments.speaker: hero
segments.text: Keep her steady, Titan,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: you say, peering over the wicker edge.

segments.speaker: hero
segments.text: Look for an entrance.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Titan set the balloon down on a snowy ledge right in front of a colossal, rusted vault door built directly into the cliff face. Above the door was a hand-painted wooden sign with crooked white lettering:

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: PRIVATE PROPERTY. KEEP OUT. THIS MEANS YOU, NUTCRACKERS. AND ESPECIALLY YOU, SANTA.

segments.speaker: pip
segments.text: This is Barnaby's workshop,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Titan whispered, his big black-spotted ears twitching nervously.

segments.speaker: pip
segments.text: He doesn't like visitors. Or noise. Or people who touch his stuff.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Pip hopped out of the basket onto the snow, puffing his green trench coat out with grandiose pride.

segments.speaker: pip
segments.text: Nonsense!

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Pip declared, adjusting his houndstooth cap.

segments.speaker: pip
segments.text: Master Detective Pip possesses the diplomatic charm of a seasoned ambassador! A simple, professional knocking sequence shall alert our grumpy friend to my prestigious arrival!

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Pip strutted up to the iron door. Beside the latch sat an antique, carved wooden clown head with an open brass horn in its mouth.

segments.speaker: pip
segments.text: Do not fear, recruit,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Pip said, winking at you.

segments.speaker: pip
segments.text: Watch the master at work.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Pip leaned forward and gave the horn a mighty, confident HONK.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: AHOOOOO-GA!

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: A shower of red sparks shot out of the clown's ears. Deep inside the canyon walls, a massive tripwire snapped with a violent TWANG!

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: CLICK-CLACK. CLICK-CLACK.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The sound didn't come from the door. It came from the snowy scrap heaps all around you.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Snow began sliding down the piles of rusted gears. Crawling out from beneath broken clock towers and hollow brass bells were dozens of wooden figures.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: They weren't Nutcrackers. They were Scrap Goblins—two-foot-tall figures carved out of rough, weathered cedar and pine. They had long, spindly wooden arms with carved claws, pointed wooden noses, and hollow red-glass eyes that flickered like dying embers.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Their wooden jaws clicked open and shut in rhythmic, unnerving synchronization:

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: CLACK-CLACK. SNAP-CLACK.

segments.speaker: pip
segments.text: Oh dear,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Pip whispered, his British accent evaporating in a microsecond.

segments.speaker: pip
segments.text: Those... those do not look like diplomatic welcoming dignitaries.

segments.speaker: pip
segments.text: TRESPASSERS DETECTED!

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: the wooden goblins hissed in scratchy, wooden voices like sandpaper rubbing on bark.

segments.speaker: pip
segments.text: INTRUDERS AT THE THRESHOLD! CHOP! CHOP! SPLINTER THEM TO KINDLING!

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Dozens of them scrambled down the junk heaps, surrounding the balloon ledge!

segments.speaker: hero
segments.text: Titan! In the basket!

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: you yell, backing toward the iron door.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Titan scrambled out of the basket to stand beside you, his massive muscular body shaking like a bowl of jelly.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: I-I-I don't like their faces! Why are their teeth so pointy?! I am having a major emotional setback!

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: You examine the heavy iron door behind you. Beside the latch is a brass puzzle-dial with three symbols: a Cog, a Bell, and a Key. To open the door, you need to solve the combination, but the wooden horde is twenty feet away and closing fast!

segments.speaker: hero
segments.text: Titan!

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: you whisper urgently, looking at his towering, ninety-pound muscular frame.

segments.speaker: hero
segments.text: They're just little toys! Stand in front of the door! Show them your teeth! Act scary!

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Titan blinked his big, soulful brown eyes.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: S-Scary? Me? But I'm a gentle soul! I participate in mindfulness!

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Just growl! Make a mean face!

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The swarm of wooden goblins froze in their tracks, suddenly noticing the colossal white bulldog standing over you. For a second, his sheer size genuinely intimidated them.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Titan took a deep, trembling breath. He puffed out his massive chest. He tried to wrinkle his nose to look ferocious.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Instead of a terrifying roar, Titan let out an apologetic, high-pitched:

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: ...AWOOF?

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He smiled a nervous, droopy-jowled smile and his little docked tail gave a hopeful, friendly twitch.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The wooden goblins blinked their red-glass eyes.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: THE BEAST IS DEFICIENT IN FEROCITY!

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: the lead goblin shrieked.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: SWARM! SWARM AND SPLINTER!

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: They lunged forward, wooden claws outstretched!

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: You have about five seconds while Titan tries to block the path with his body! You need to input the right sequence on Barnaby's door dial!

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: What symbol on the door dial do you turn first to crack Barnaby's defense lock?

c4p4.title: The Last Stand & The Door Opens

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: You remember the entry in the Clockmaker's journal:

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Barnaby forged the primary escapement with three cogs.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: You grab the brass dial and spin it hard toward the COG symbol!

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: CLIIIICK-WHIRRRRRR!

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Inside the stone doorframe, heavy internal weights drop with a thunderous THUD. The heavy iron bolt slides back, and the massive door cracks open three inches!

segments.speaker: hero
segments.text: The door is unlocking!

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: you shout.

segments.speaker: hero
segments.text: Titan, get inside!

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: I'M TRYING TO BE BRAVE!

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Titan whimpered, backing against the wall with his paws up.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The wooden goblins surged up the snowy steps! Two of them lunged straight for your boots, their carved wooden claws snapping like bear traps!

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Pip frantically shoved his shoulder against the iron door, trying to push it open.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Titan saw the claws snapping inches from your legs. Something deep inside the giant bulldog snapped. His terrified whimpering stopped. His droopy ears flattened against his skull.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He didn't care about the dark. He didn't care about the creepy faces.

segments.speaker: narrator

segments.text: It... it didn't take,

segments.text: Who are the Unbound?

segments.text: Barnaby walked around his workbench and looked up at you.
